title: Dungeon Hoard - Build the Dungeon, Stop the Heroes (Game Crafter)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wnahjxPk5rk

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *Dungeon Hoard*, Ernest Fosa's Game Crafter card game (review copy) in the *Dungeon Keeper* vein: you are the villain, building a lair of up to five rooms with your treasure room at the far end, and the first player to fill three chests, fifteen loot bags in all, wins. He is candid that it is not a solo game and would not work as one; its take-that heart needs opponents. He is playing two-handed to learn it for his casual group.

Each turn: draw a dungeon card, build a room or attach a creature above it or an upgrade below it, then draw an event. Most events send adventurers crawling room by room; that deck also holds level-ups, so a levelled, buffed cleric with foolish courage arrived at power five. Zombies are too slow to strike back if beaten; tasty poisonous mushrooms cost two damage unless the party has a druid or ranger; an impossible riddle stops any party lacking a wizard, bard or enough will. The second player's lair stacks dead ends behind a labyrinth to buy building time, then a crocodile in an underground lake. Immediate cards are the mischief: heal an intruder in a rival's dungeon, hand them a map straight to the treasure room, or hide your stash.

Daniel enjoys the humour and thinks it avoids *Munchkin*'s endless endgame. He calls it a strong prototype a publisher should pick up.

----

Fancy playing the dungeon for once? Which villain-side game has actually made you feel like the monster?
